text_devanagari: धी॒ती वा॒ ये अन॑यद्वा॒चो अयं॒ मन॑सा वा॒ ये ऽव॑दन्नृ॒तानि॑ । ॥ १ ॥
y_bands: All y in leaf-block coordinates (text block = crop (482,362)-(3618,5448) of the 4000 px leaf; block 3136x5086). Measured by row-ink projection at ink threshold 140; the verso bleed-through ghost is never darker than gray 183 anywhere in these bands, so ghost and ink are fully separable and no band boundary rests on a judgement call. LINE-ABOVE BAR BAND: line 1 is the short centred ॥ ओं ॥ and its ink lies only in y1737-1854; its own bar band would fall near y1885-1900, and I measured y1855-1914 as ZERO ink at every x. On this line the line-above trap is therefore empirically absent - nothing from line 1 can reach my bands. MY SVARITA BAND: y1914-1951 (the four upright strokes begin at y1914-1920 and stand on the sirorekha at 1951, with clean white above them). MY SIROREKHA: y1950-1967; row-ink peak 2119 px at y1963, solid 1953-1966. MY GLYPH BODY: y1968-2032. MY DESCENDER/SUBSCRIPT ZONE: y2033-2058 (the द tail in वदन्नृ, the ृ hook). MY OWN ANUDATTA BAR BAND: y2058-2072 - five bars at 2059-2068, 2061-2069, 2061-2069, 2061-2071, 2062-2072 - plus ONE bar dropped to y2076-2086 because the ृ hook of न्नृ occupies the normal band there. NEXT LINE (line 3): above-headline band y2091-2126, sirorekha y2127-2143, body y2144-2209, descender zone y2210-2237, its own bar band y2238-2261 (ordinary bars 2239-2250, and two bars dropped to 2250-2261 under the ृ of तृ and वृ - the same displacement rule, which is what corroborates my sixth bar). Line pitch 177 px (sirorekha centre 1958 -> 2135); the bar band sits +103..+114 below its own sirorekha, +118..+128 when a ृ pushes it down.
boundary_interpretation: WORDS. I took word boundaries from where the sirorekha itself breaks, sampled at rows 1956/1960/1963. Inter-word gaps measure 39-51 px; gaps between aksaras inside a word measure 6-23 px, so the two classes do not overlap. Printed words with x spans: 0 धीती 190-409 (the 223-229 break is internal to ध, whose curl and right stem separate below the headline), 1 वा 449-566, 2 ये 607-679, 3 अनयद्वाचो 720-1210, 4 अयं 1249-1431, 5 मनसा 1470-1744, 6 वा 1784-1903, 7 ये 1942-2015, 8 ऽवदन्नृतानि 2061-2562, 9 । 2606-2622, 10 ॥ १ ॥ 2875-3096. The avagraha ऽ (2061-2109) is separated from the following व by only 11 px at headline level (23 px in the body zone), i.e. an inter-aksara gap and not a word space, so I treat ऽवदन्नृतानि as one printed word (word_index 8). The avagraha is a sign of elision, not an aksara, so it gets no aksara_index: inside word 8 the indices are व=0, द=1, न्नृ=2, ता=3, नि=4. AKSARAS. Boundaries come from a column-ink profile of the body zone y1972-2032 - below the sirorekha, so the headline cannot bridge them. Runs: 195-252 + 269-287 (धी), 306-358 + 377-395 (ती) | 461-517 + 540-556 (वा) | 617-674 (ये) | 723-812 (अ), 824-887 (न), 902-959 (य), 966-1036 + 1054-1070 (द्वा), 1092-1157 + 1180-1197 (चो) | 1252-1343 (अ), 1354-1422 (यं) | 1477-1547 (म), 1557-1620 (न), 1627-1696 + 1714-1731 (सा) | 1796-1852 + 1874-1890 (वा) | 1951-2009 (ये) | 2061-2109 (ऽ), 2133-2189 (व), 2201-2253 (द), 2259-2332 (न्नृ), 2346-2401 + 2421-2441 (ता), 2461-2479 + 2492-2555 (नि). MARKS NEAR A BOUNDARY - side assigned, and why. (a) svarita x866-877 in word 3: it stands over the right stem of न, whose body run is 824-887; the next aksara य does not start until 902, behind a 14 px empty valley (888-901). Assigned to न, not य. (b) svarita x1601-1613 in मनसा: over the right stem of न (1557-1620); स starts at 1627. Assigned to न. (c) svarita x2537-2548 in word 8: over the न of नि. The i-matra stroke is set to the LEFT (2461-2479) and the न to the right (2492-2555), but the two are one aksara नि, so the mark is interior to it; ता ends at 2441 and the danda does not begin until 2606. Assigned to नि. (d) anudatta x1380-1419 in अयं: it sits under य (1354-1422), which also carries the anusvara dot at 1398-1421 directly above it. अ ends at 1343. Assigned to यं; I note explicitly that the bar and the dot are on the same aksara and are two different signs. (e) anudatta x2293-2329 in word 8: under the न्नृ conjunct (2259-2332); द ends at 2253 and ता does not start until 2346. Assigned to न्नृ. (f) anudatta x996-1032 in word 3: under the द्व part of द्वा (966-1036, with its a-stem at 1054-1070); य ends at 959. Assigned to द्वा. No mark straddles a word space, and no mark lies closer to a neighbouring aksara's ink than to its own.
notes: MAGNIFICATION. I worked from the two supplied 1:1 segment crops, then re-rendered my own ruled windows from the 4000 px leaf via crop_atharvaveda_leaf.find_text_block / leaf_path: eight windows of 420x194 block px at 3.6x, then targeted zooms at 4.2-9.4x and one 16.7x view of the न्न stack. Beyond roughly 2x this is interpolation, and I used it only for spatial judgement, never as new detail. Every count is from measurement rather than from the rendered picture: 8-connected component extraction on the leaf block at ink thresholds 90 / 110 / 140 / 170 / 190, plus row and column ink profiles. The mark inventory is identical at thresholds 110 and 170, so nothing here depends on where I set the threshold. REJECTED FALSE POSITIVES - by shape, not by position. (1) Six wide curved matras above the headline, centres x257, x365, x638, x1155, x1972, x2492, measuring 53-72 px across and 28-34 px tall: the ी of धी and of ती, the े of both ये, the ो of चो, the ि of नि. Wide curved shapes, not narrow strokes, so not svarita. (2) The mark at x1398-1421, y1924-1949: w24, h25, aspect 0.96, ink fill 0.70, diamond-shaped, and it does not touch the sirorekha. An anusvara on यं of अयं. Round dot about as wide as it is tall, so not svarita - even though it sits directly above an anudatta bar and could be read as a paired accent. (3) The descender at x2249-2266, y2030-2057, h27, aspect 1.5: the diagonal tail of द in वदन्नृ. It runs out of the glyph body with no white gap and tapers, so not a detached flat dash. (4) The descender at x2301-2343, y2030-2074, h45, aspect 0.96: the ृ hook of न्नृ - exactly the vocalic-r false positive the brief names, a curved hook rather than a straight dash. (5) Eight small stubs clipped at the body-zone floor near x1192, 1665, 1849, 1886, 2183, 2433, 2550, 3004: all 2-6 px tall and continuous with the glyph body above them, i.e. glyph feet, not detached bars. (6) Faint smudges that appear only at thresholds 170-190, at x2074 (y2068-2073) and x2535 (y2072-2081): both roundish (aspect 1.0-2.7) and both gone at threshold 140, whereas every real bar is solid at threshold 90. Verso bleed-through, rejected. THE SIXTH ANUDATTA - the one real judgement call, and how I settled it. The bar at x2293-2329 sits at y2076-2086, about 14 px below the band the other five occupy, and at threshold 140 it merges with the ृ hook of न्नृ into a single component. At threshold 90 it separates cleanly: w35, h8, aspect 4.4, 236 ink px - the same size, shape and density class as the five undisputed bars (w33-37, h6-9, aspect 3.9-5.5, 193-265 ink px). It cannot come from the line above: line 1 is the short centred ॥ ओं ॥, nowhere near x2311, and y1855-1914 is empty at every x. It cannot come from line 3, whose sirorekha does not begin until y2127 and whose own bar band lies at y2238-2261. Decisive corroboration from the print's own habit: on line 3 the bars under तृ (x88-121) and वृ (x1226-1260) are likewise dropped to y2250-2261 while its ordinary bars sit at y2239-2250. This fount drops the anudatta clear of a ृ hook, so I count this one. Without it the answer would be 5 anudatta; I record the displacement explicitly so the disagreement, if any, is locatable. READINGS I HAD TO WORK FOR. The 1856 standalone अ does read as ऋ or श्र to a modern eye (brief's fount note); I read it as अ at x723-812 and x1252-1343, and the two forms are identical to each other and to the अ of the running head. Two stacked conjuncts needed comparison against unambiguous letters elsewhere on the same scan rather than guesswork: x966-1070 I read द्वा, because its upper member repeats the left wedge plus rightward bar of the plain द at x2201-2253 and its lower member repeats the closed loop of the plain व at x2133-2189; x2259-2332 I read न्नृ, because at 16.7x it is visibly two identical न hook-and-bar forms stacked on a shared right stem. I also checked the first aksara against line 3's ध in धेनोः (x2065-2135), which shows the same left flag, 3-shaped double curl and right stem, confirming धी and not some other flagged letter. WHAT I DID NOT DO. I consulted no text, edition, translation or web resource, and I did not open the detector scripts, the transcription data, the baseline run file, or any other reader's directory. धीती and अनयद्वाचो are what the ink shows; I did not bend them toward any remembered Atharvaveda wording, and I did not try to make the accent pattern satisfy a grammatical expectation. UNRESOLVED. Nothing material. The ॥ १ ॥ at x2875-3096 is set off to the right with 253 px of space after the single danda at x2606-2622, and I have kept both as printed. Residual risk, stated plainly: the identity of the two stacked conjuncts is an inference from letterform comparison at a resolution close to the scan's limit, but neither affects any mark count or any carrier assignment.
